findings.where: venue waterfront_pier_nine review 2 (last sentence), venue waterfront_keel_street review 1 (brother sentence), venue waterfront_tidewater review 2 (last sentence)
findings.issue: The 'relative with the need' device has crept back. Four of the seven venues now prove a need through someone close to the reviewer: Pier Nine's brother-in-law (peanut), Keel Street's brother (dairy), Bluewater's daughter (peanut) and Quayside's brother's groom (peanut), with Tidewater's 'friend whose stomach turns at a splash of milk' as a fifth. Levels 17 and 18 already leaned on this device heavily (cousin, son, daughter, sister, husband, brother, girlfriend, boyfriend, father). Two of the four come from my own first-round wording, so this is on the critique, not the seeder. Keel Street's 'whose stomach has never forgiven milk' also nearly copies level_19 Harbour Moon ('The owner's stomach has never got on with milk') and sits next to Tidewater's 'stomach turns at a splash of milk' in this same level. Keep Bluewater's daughter and Quayside's groom, and replace the other three.
findings.suggested_fix: Pier Nine review 2: replace 'My brother-in-law, who reacts to a crumb of one, took it at its word years ago and has worked through every special since without a single bad night.' with 'The regulars read it like a timetable: the crunch on the ricotta tart is toasted hazelnut, and the bowls along the bar hold olives and taralli, never a peanut.' Keel Street review 1: replace 'My brother, whose stomach has never forgiven milk, cleared his plate and the bread basket, asked for more of the olive oil and was fine the whole next day, and I walked out feeling lighter than I walked in.' with 'Dessert gives the kitchen away as an olive-oil house through and through: the cannoli are piped with sweet almond paste instead of ricotta, the only other sweet is a blood-orange granita, and nothing on the card arrives finished with cheese. I walked out feeling lighter than I walked in.' Tidewater review 2: delete the last sentence ('My friend whose stomach turns at a splash of milk didn't ask a single question all night.'). The olive-oil baklava, the bean spreads and the capers instead of cheese already show it is dairy-free.

summary: All ten first-round fixes landed cleanly. The chat is tighter at 20 lines, Mina's first-line ask is soft and never names her diet, Cyrus's 'Off duty' / 'Mostly off duty' pair carries his arc and Roxy's hidden dairy need (clue rule 6), and Brooke's perfect line now pays off his night off. Every trap still has firm review evidence: Breakwater's baker never borrowing a peanut, Keel Street's peanut busiate, Marina Arch's meat in every main, Pier Nine's cheese and cream, Quayside's 'clear notch above', Bluewater's fryer and Tidewater's lack of pasta. The outcomes still match the rewritten reviews. The one new issue is a freshness echo: the rework turned 'a relative with the need' into the default proof at four of the seven venues. Two of those came from my own suggested wording.
